The searches, carried out across Bhubaneswar, Balasore, Jajpur, and Baliguda districts, are in response to allegations that Behera possessed assets disproportionate to his known sources of income. The operation is ongoing, with investigators examining the valuation of gold ornaments, bank deposits, investments, and other financial assets.  The total value of the assets allegedly accumulated by Behera is expected to become clearer once the searches and valuation process are completed.

recent_articles.title: Driver who allegedly dumped accident victim’s body on roadside arrested within 48 hours | The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mehboob Lakeeb Mohammad Shaikh**, a 40-year-old resident of Parner, was arrested by the **Pimpri Chinchwad police** for allegedly dumping the body of a pedestrian, **Manojkumar Ramji Vishwakarma**, after he was struck by a speeding vehicle on June 4th.  The incident occurred near Khalumbre on the Chakan–Talegaon road and the investigation revealed that Shaikh kept Vishwakarma's body in his vehicle before discarding it on the roadside in Shirur. The **North Mhalunge police station** filed an FIR under various sections of the BNS, including those related to rash driving and endangering human life, as well as the Motor Vehicles Act.

recent_articles.title: American builders made houses with puja room, spice kitchen for Indians; Trump aide says 'completely end H-1B visa' - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Brandon Gill**, a Republican, criticized the housing market decline in Texas attributed to President Donald Trump's crackdown on **H-1B visa abuse**.  **CBRE Group**, a real estate firm, confirmed that **H-1B workers** fueled the US housing boom between 2018 and present. As Indian buyers are now leaving the market, prices are decreasing in Collin County, Texas, with home prices falling nearly 9% year-over-year.  The influx of Indian-Americans into Texas has led to significant growth in Collin and Denton counties, with **Indian-born** residents averaging over 116,000 annually.

recent_articles.title: World Cup 2026: Can sub-Saharan Africa outdo noisy neighbours from north? | Football News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Sub-Saharan African nations Senegal, Ghana, Ivory Coast, and Cape Verde are looking to surpass their North African counterparts in the 2026 World Cup.  Senegal, seeking revenge for a controversial title stripping, boasts a strong squad led by Sadio Mane and Pape Gueye. Ghana faces a challenging group with England and Croatia, while Ivory Coast aims to build on its recent AFCON success. Cape Verde, making their debut, will face Uruguay, Saudi Arabia, and Spain in a daunting group.  DR Congo returns after a 1974 appearance, seeking to make an impact in the tournament.

recent_articles.title: 'Beer should be better in 2026': WC to boost global sales by a billion pints
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A study by **Jefferies**, an investment bank, predicts that the 2026 FIFA World Cup will boost global beer consumption by one billion pints. The expanded tournament format with more matches and games in favorable time zones is expected to drive increased sales, particularly for companies like **Anheuser-Busch InBev** and **Heineken**.  The economic impact of the event, including tourism and GDP growth, is projected to be significant but may not have lasting effects.

recent_articles.title: Eye on monsoon, PWD directs all its divisions to complete drain cleaning and desilting work by June 15 | Delhi News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Public Works Department (PWD)** has ordered all its divisions to complete drain cleaning and desilting work by June 15th to prevent flooding in Delhi. **Water Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh** inspected a waterlogging hotspot, the Zakhira underpass, and emphasized that the government is strengthening infrastructure and improving drainage systems before the monsoon arrives.  The PWD has directed engineers to ensure proper evidence of drain cleaning and timely removal of silt, as well as coordinate with other departments for regular cleaning of drains and manholes.

recent_articles.title: The World This Week | Nepal PM raises India border dispute, war in Lebanon casts shadow on US-Iran truce, Trump’s ‘new’ tariffs | UPSC Current Affairs News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Nepal’s newly elected Prime Minister, Balendra Shah, reignited a long-standing border dispute with India by claiming that both countries have encroached on each other's territory.  Shah suggested reaching out to China and the United Kingdom for resolution, while India's foreign ministry spokesperson rejected third-party intervention. Meanwhile, US-Iran ceasefire talks stalled due to Israel’s ongoing campaign in Lebanon, leading to a heated exchange between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and US President Donald Trump. The US Trade Representative proposed imposing tariffs on 60 countries, including India, for failing to enforce prohibitions against forced labor.

recent_articles.title: 'Very happy for Shreyas': Surya on Iyer succeeding him as India T20I captain
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rohit Sharma**, **Suryakumar Yadav**, and **Shreyas Iyer** were all involved in recent developments within the Indian cricket team.  **Yadav**, who led India to victory in the 2023 T20 World Cup, was replaced as captain by **Iyer**. recent_articles.title: 13.5 Million Km, 80,000 Words: Shubhanshu Shukla Brings Space Down To Earth
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla**, a decorated Indian Air Force pilot and test pilot, has published his memoir "The Second Orbit" shortly after returning from the Axiom-4 Mission. The book explores the emotional journey of an astronaut, focusing on doubt, belief, and persistence.  Shukla's writing reflects not only the science and spectacle of spaceflight but also the inner life of an astronaut.  Endorsements for the book highlight its significance, with India's first astronaut, Rakesh Sharma, calling it a "master class" and Sachin Tendulkar praising its inspirational quality. The book underscores the collective aspiration tied to India's space program and is being published by Penguin Books at the end of this month.
